title: Bijectivity of the canonical Kähler differential map modulo a power
statement: Under the quotient algebra structure S/I^(n+1) → S/I^n, the canonical (S/I^n)-linear map from (S/I^n) ⊗[S] Ω[S/R] to (S/I^n) ⊗[S/I^(n+1)] Ω[S/I^(n+1)] sending t ⊗ ds to t ⊗ d(s mod I^(n+1)) is bijective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal, line 34194); its proof: Lemma Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq, line 34103) and d(I^{n+1}) contained in I^n Omega_{S/R} by the Leibniz rule

proof.text: Apply the conormal exact sequence for S → S/I^(n+1), tensor it with S/I^n, identify the middle term by tensor cancellation, and use d(I^(n+1)) ⊆ I^n Ω[S/R] from the Leibniz rule to show the resulting map has zero kernel and is surjective.

lean.statement:
theorem kahlerDifferential_mod_power_ideal_bijective
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (I : Ideal S) (n : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    letI : Algebra (S ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)) (S ⧸ I ^ n) :=
      (Ideal.Quotient.factorPowSucc I n).toAlgebra
    ∃ f : (S ⧸ I ^ n) ⊗[S] KaehlerDifferential R S →ₗ[S ⧸ I ^ n]
        (S ⧸ I ^ n) ⊗[S ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)]
          KaehlerDifferential R (S ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)),
      Function.Bijective f ∧
      ∀ (s t : S),
        f (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n) t ⊗ₜ[S] KaehlerDifferential.D R S s) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n) t ⊗ₜ[S ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)]
            KaehlerDifferential.D R (S ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))
              (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)) s)
